And they sent two persons as envoys to the Catholicos:
one an Arab, and the other an Armenian.
And they said to him:
"The Sultan has commanded that you surrender the fortress peacefully,
and take your monks and go dwell in Jerusalem,
and he will give you villages sufficient for your maintenance.
And if you do not want this,
but wish to go to Cilicia,
likewise on our mules and horses we will convey you with honor.
But if you resist and do not surrender,
God will require the blood of all these Christians from you!"
The Catholicos, however, replied:
"Until I die, I will fight,
and I will not be unfaithful to God and to the king."
Then all that night the Egyptians went around in the orchards,
and cut down trees,
and prepared ladders.
And in the morning of Saturday they launched a fierce attack against the city,
and they put to flight the Armenians who were fighting on that new wall which they had built below.
And they set up the ladders,
and entered the wretched city, and plundered it,
and burned all its houses.
And because all its people had fled above into the citadel,
they did not find anyone in the city.
However, for five days they remained in it,
plundering, taking captives, and burning.
Then they departed from it, after the great devastation which they had wrought in it;
and they consumed its crops,
and cut down its vineyards and its trees,
and broke the millstones,
and uprooted the boilers of the baths and took them away to Aleppo.
And in those days,
while the army of the Egyptians was encamped against Qal'ah Rumaytā (Hromgla),
the son of Qaramān the Turkmen sent an envoy from the territory of the Romans (Anatolia) to the master of Egypt (the Sultan),
asking him to send him troops to clear the road before him and bring him over into Syria,
because {OCR: ܡܛܠ} he was afraid of the forces of the Tatars and of the king of the Armenians.
And the master of Egypt sent to King Leon,
asking him to grant passage to Amir Baysari to go and bring the son of Qaramān.
The king consented
that they should pass through the borders of his land.
And they did so.
And they passed through the mountains and came out near Caesarea,
and they took the son of Qaramān and returned.
